annotations.title: Film an animation frame by frame

description: Runs the game on a virtual clock, optionally performs steps to trigger something, then films it frame by frame. Returns a contact sheet (tiles with frame number and time, dashed boxes around what moved, a bar per frame of how much changed) and an onion-skin image (the whole motion ghosted into one picture), plus flagged sudden jumps, one-frame flicker and stalls. Runs are deterministic: pass compare = the folder of an earlier run to see exactly what a code change did.

area.description: CSS selector of the game area (default: the largest canvas)

compare.description: Output folder of an earlier frames run to compare with

duration.description: How long to film, e.g. 800ms or 1.5s (default 1s)

fps.description: Tiles per second on the sheet (default: fit about 24 tiles)

ready.description: JavaScript expression that is true once the game has loaded

scenario.description: Name of a scenario in playproof.config.json: supplies steps, duration, zoom and device

steps.description: Steps separated by ";". Steps (separate with ";" or new lines, "#" starts a comment line): wait <time> let time pass (virtual time: instant and exact) tap <x,y>|@label tap/click inside the game area ("50%,80%" or pixels "120,300") press <x,y> <time> long press drag <x,y> <x,y> [time] swipe/drag (default 300ms) key <Key> [time] press a key, e.g. Space, ArrowLeft, a, Enter (held 50ms by default) type <text> type text click <css selector> click a DOM element (menus, HTML buttons) shot [label] take a screenshot for the storyboard film <time> [fps] capture frames while time passes until <js expression> [time] advance time until the expression is truthy (default timeout 5s) js <js expression> evaluate JavaScript in the page and log the result Times: 500, 500ms, 1.5s.

target.description: URL (e.g. http://localhost:5173), folder (./dist) or HTML file of the game. Optional when playproof.config.json sets it.

waitFor.description: CSS selector to wait for before starting

zoom.description: Crop to what moves ("auto") or to x,y,w,h in percent of the game area

name: frames
